explain.say: The Han rulers pushed the wall west into the Gobi Desert. With no stone there, they used layers of reeds and gravel, and some still stand today! Now look at 1368: the Ming rulers. What do you think they used?

faq.q: How long is the Great Wall?
faq.a: A survey in 2012 measured all the sections built over the centuries at about 21,196 kilometres. The best-known Ming wall is about 8,850 kilometres.
asks: What is the length of the Great Wall?

faq.q: Who built the first Great Wall?
faq.a: Small states built walls from the 600s BCE. Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of China, joined many of them into one long wall after 221 BCE.

faq.q: How did guards on the wall send messages?
faq.a: They lit fires at night and made smoke in the day on watchtowers. The signal passed from tower to tower much faster than a rider could go.

faq.q: Can you see the Great Wall from space?
faq.a: Not with your eyes alone. It is very long but only a few metres wide, about the same colour as the land around it. China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, said he could not see it.
asks: Is the Great Wall visible from the Moon?

faq.a: Ming builders mixed soup made from sticky rice into lime mortar. The rice made the mortar stronger and more waterproof.
asks: Did they use rice to build the Great Wall?

facts: A 2012 Chinese government survey measured all Great Wall sections at about 21,196 kilometres.
Ming dynasty builders used sticky rice mixed into lime mortar to strengthen walls.
